reason: A-panel packing and scratch-lifetime changes target the existing per-call packing cost; transpose fusion may also avoid scratch traffic, though it risks repeating work. Traversal and cache-layout proposals have plausible reuse effects but no evidence that cache behavior is limiting. I rank B-panel packing mid-list: the current paired loads already read each 32-column B segment contiguously, so packing adds setup and 64 KiB of panel storage without a clear access improvement. Store grouping and scheduling changes may help, but require exact assembler and mapping checks. Prior K-loop variants were not promoted; their noisy outcomes do not establish a general effect. The fallback-only tail change has little relevance to timed n=512.
